assessment: The applied swap block (HISTORY.md, decklist fb99de15993a) emptied this bench of its step-up package: what remains is fourteen conditional answers plus the seven fair bodies the block sent down, and the sideboard's job has changed from 'upgrade path' to 'answer box plus one live trial'. The computed floor is now 4, driven by the combo DB tagging Polyraptor + Forerunner of the Empire a two-card infinite — while stack 003 verified that exact pairing as a bounded, self-terminating burst of at most seven tokens (the engine does not consult passing stacks; hapatra precedent), so the honest framing is floor 4 with a verified-reality argument for 3. One promotion remains live on the evidence: Bellowing Aegisaur into the now-maindeck, stack-005-verified ping web. The loudest fact on the bench is negative: Marauding Raptor now sits one promotion away from importing the stack-002 verified whole-table draw, because its Polyraptor partner is in the 99.

swaps.when: Pods where the ping web is the operating plan — damage-sweeper and attrition tables — and as a trial promotion until the Aegisaur-under-multi-ping survival-budget scenario is run (see gaps); its verdict below stays keep-in-sideboard because this is conditional, not a default.
swaps.why: Its v1 blocker — 'a 6-mana 5/5 that needs someone else to hurt it' — is resolved: the someone else is now maindeck and verified, with the enrage engine drawn 72.1% by turn 6 (goldfish v2) and stack 005 showing the web re-arming on every Dinosaur ETB, so each optional Forerunner ping reads 'put a +1/+1 counter on each other creature you control' — permanent counters that harden the 1/3 Forerunner hub the frame names as outside every tribal protection layer (it died to its own third sweep in stack 003), and under the stack-004 one-sided Blasphemous Act the 1 damage Aegisaur takes turns the sweep into a team anthem; Pugnacious Hammerskull is the maindeck's only zero-trigger pure-stats body — the one axis a 34-body deck never lacks, the argument that already benched Rampaging Brontodon — and its stun clause is live exactly on post-wrath rebuild turns when you control no other Dinosaur. The full composite is oracle-text arithmetic on verified pieces, not yet a passed stack: the opens_lines entry carries needs-a-scenario.

citations.quote: buy resilience instead of restraint where you can

opens_lines.why_plausible: THE WARNING LINE, now one promotion from live: Polyraptor is maindeck, so sleeving Marauding Raptor imports this directly. Verified as a mandatory loop — Marauding's 2-damage ping and Polyraptor's copy trigger are both mandatory, 2 never kills a fresh 5/5 token, the deck has no sacrifice outlet or free loop-breaker — that DRAWS the whole game for all players (CR 732.4/104.4b) unless an opponent chooses to intervene. A liability, not a wincon.

Now fully maindeck — the contained line behind the floor-4 computation. The combo DB tags it a two-card infinite; the stack verified the real ceiling: Forerunner's ping is 'you may', the burst self-terminates when Forerunner dies to its own third sweep, maximum SEVEN tokens (reached by declining one intermediate trigger; yes-to-everything caps at six), safely stoppable at every link. Bounded, controllable, not infinite — the honest bracket framing the artifacts carry.

Now fully maindeck. Verified one-sided sweep: your other Dinosaurs are each dealt exactly 1 under Temple Altisaur, Temple eats its own 13 and dies but still converts to a 13-point redirect via last known information, SBAs clear opponents' creatures before redirect targets are chosen, and 16 total damage goes at a player (40 to 10 — not lethal from 26).

The applied board's engine, verified in situ: one optional ping off a single Dinosaur ETB yields an opponent's 1/1 dead to SBAs, their 3/3 exiled under Trapjaw Tyrant, a Ripjaw draw, a Ranging Raptors tapped Forest, and a Polyraptor copy token whose own ETB re-arms Forerunner with a genuinely new optional trigger — cost, 1 damage marked on each of your creatures, all surviving.

The frame's open question, both halves now maindeck but never verified on one board: stack 005's web resolved without Wrathful out, stack 004 shows Wrathful converting damage to your Dinosaurs into redirects. Whether a Forerunner ping with Wrathful on the battlefield still marks damage on your Dinosaurs (enrage triggers AND free reach) or is somehow turned into redirects (dead engine) turns on Wrathful's exact wording — unresolved rules work the frame declines to guess at.

The frame's quantification gap: Selvala tapping for X>=5 plus Behemoth's doubled land taps plausibly casts Gishath two-plus turns ahead of the 7.982 goldfish mean, but the simulator models neither card (stated assumption) — no artifact quantifies the acceleration, so the manual may not state a number until a goldfish extension or worked sequencing scenario exists.

Each optional ping should put a +1/+1 counter on each OTHER creature you control — a team anthem per Dinosaur ETB that also grows the fragile Forerunner hub — but Aegisaur itself never grows and eats every ping (five sweeps of a 003-style burst kill a 5/5), so its survival budget mid-burst is exactly what needs verifying before the trial swap above becomes a default.
Each optional ping should make each opponent sacrifice a permanent of their choice — a repeatable triple edict per Dinosaur ETB — if Silverclad's enrage triggers off the 1 damage; unverified.

Each optional ping should read 'this 10/10 fights up to one target creature you don't control', and fight-back damage should re-trigger its own enrage for a chained second fight, bounded by its 10-toughness budget — repeatable removal every Dinosaur ETB, the strongest case the card has ever had here, but the chain has never been run.

long_term_defaults.why: WARNING — promotion is now blocked outright, not merely conditional: Polyraptor is MAINDECK, so sleeving Marauding Raptor imports the stack-002 verified mandatory loop that draws the whole game (CR 732.4/104.4b) directly into the 99, and the deck has no sacrifice outlet or free breaker. The swap-8 branch (Marauding for Otepec in a Polyraptor-less build) is dead in the applied build; promotion requires Polyraptor leaving the 99 or a free sac outlet arriving first, and even then its mandatory 2-ping kills Intrepid Paleontologist and the remaining 1-toughness utility bodies on entry. Bracket if added: 4, no change (sideboard-facts) — the DB's Marauding line is a draw machine, not a wincon.

Benched by swap 1 for Selvala. Return case: enchantment- or artifact-stax pods where a fourth Naturalize body matters — the 99 keeps Thrashing Brontodon, Zacama, and Beast Within on that axis, so it returns only when answer density outbids the mana tier that displaced it.

Benched by swap 2 for Regal Behemoth. Return case: racing and burn pods where life total is the axis — and it is livelier than when it left: each 5-toughness Polyraptor token of a stack-003 burst would be 5 life, up to 35-plus off one ETB. Still 7 mana that rebuilds nothing after a wrath, and anti-synergic with Rampaging Ferocidon if that hate card is ever sleeved alongside it.

Benched by swap 3 for Forerunner of the Empire. Return case: thin — team double strike converts boards that are already winning, the reason it left; alongside Rampaging Brontodon it holds the weakest return case on the bench.

Benched by swap 4 for Polyraptor. Return case: destroy-sweeper attrition metas wanting an indestructible body that survives everything short of exile — but at 8 mana it competes with Gishath's own slot for the deck's one big cast per game, the argument that benched it.

Benched by swap 5 for Wrathful Raptors. Return case: only if the draw suite thins — its ETB pays off exactly the wide board Gishath's reveal creates, which is draw after the board is already won; win-more where the 99 needs setup.

Benched by swap 6 for Ranging Raptors. Return case: pods that punish slow starts, where a turn-2 any-colour body outbids sweeper exposure — at 3/3 with a Dinosaur out it survives a single Forerunner ping, but it still dies to the deck's own Blasphemous Act, the wrath-math reason ramp moved onto lands.

Benched by swap 7 for Trapjaw Tyrant. Return case: haste-heavy aggro pods — opponents' creatures entering tapped is real tempo — accepting that a 1/2 dies to the second ping of any multi-ping turn, including the deck's own stack-003 burst.

The one live trial promotion (see swaps): its v1 blocker is gone — the deck now reliably hurts it (web maindeck, enrage engine 72.1% drawn by t6) — but the anthem-per-ping composite and its survival budget mid-burst are unverified, so it is a conditional sleeve for web-centric pods until the named stack scenario runs, not a default.

Its best case ever: with the web maindeck each ping should be a 10/10 fighting a creature you don't control (opens_lines, unverified). Still {7}{G}{G} in a top band where Zacama does repeatable removal with strictly more modes and mean available mana is 5.497 at t6; sleeve it for creature-mirror pods, not by default.

The verdict already priced in a full ping web and the web arriving maindeck does not change the magnitude: 2 damage at a face per ping is real reach but too small to displace a maindeck three-slot in a 40-life format, and its 2 toughness dies to the second sweep of any stack-003 burst after dealing only 4.

The ping-to-triple-edict line is still unverified (opens_lines), and at 7 mana with no protection it is a slow payoff in the deck's most crowded band; the scenario run would move it to the trial tier, not the bench door.
Draws only off opponents' non-mana creature and land activations — a meta call for fetchland and activated-ability pods, blank elsewhere; nothing in the applied block touches its math.
Graveyard hate the maindeck already partially covers with Intrepid Paleontologist's exile activation; sleeve it against reanimator pods.

Token and lifegain hate whose costs went UP with the applied block: 'players can't gain life' still hits your own Vaultborn Tyrant, and its ETB ping now punishes your own engine — every Polyraptor token of a stack-003 burst deals 1 damage to YOU, up to 7 per burst. Sleeve only where opposing tokens or lifegain dominate the pod.

Copying your best Dinosaur on attack still requires already having the best Dinosaur and surviving to combat at 2/2-equivalent rate; copying maindeck Polyraptor is a cute second enrage copier but the same win-more shape.

A 7-mana attack-only pump body with no ETB, no draw, and no enrage — raw stats remain the one axis this 34-body deck never lacks, the same argument the Aegisaur swap uses against Pugnacious Hammerskull.

A fourth reducer that lands turn 4 and saves mana only from turn 5 on, behind Urza's Incubator, Otepec Huntmaster, and Huatli in the same job; the applied mana tier (Selvala, Behemoth) attacks the 8-drop problem harder than another reducer would.
Turn-1 W on 9 white land sources is unreliable, and a 1/2 Human — outside Temple Altisaur's Dinosaur-only prevention — is collateral to the deck's own multi-ping turns.
Basic landcycling for {2} is honest early flexibility for a 21-land deck, but as a body it is a fair 6-mana trampler with no trigger in the band the web upgrades made most competitive.
A spare physical copy — the card is already in the 99 and singleton rules make promoting the duplicate illegal; a backup, not an option.

gaps: No bench card has an EDHREC rank (sideboard-facts note), so every verdict above rests on this deck's needs, the five passing stacks, and oracle text rather than popularity; nothing settles this short of ranks appearing in a data refresh.

The computed floor 4 rests on the combo DB's infinite tag for Polyraptor + Forerunner of the Empire, which stack 003 verified as bounded at seven tokens and self-terminating — the bracket engine does not consult passing stacks (known limitation, hapatra precedent), so the artifacts must keep carrying floor 4 with the verified-reality argument for 3 until the engine consumes stack verdicts.

One /resolve-stack run on the ping web with Bellowing Aegisaur (survival budget under multi-ping, counters on Forerunner) would settle the trial swap; a second on Silverclad Ferocidons and the Apex Altisaur fight-chain would settle the last two candidate composites. Each is one rules domain and should be its own scenario.

Wrathful Raptors x the ping web (redirect versus enrage on your own Dinosaurs) is the frame's named unresolved rules question — both halves are maindeck, no stack has run them on one board, and no verdict here guesses at it.

Selvala/Regal Behemoth acceleration is unquantified: the goldfish models neither card, so the 7.982 mean cast is the floor of the problem, not the expectation; a goldfish model extension or worked sequencing scenario is needed before any manual states a number.

The strategy corpus still has no section on typal construction, enrage/self-damage engines, or Commander upgrade-path doctrine (logged in strategic_frame.gaps) — the verdicts here lean on critical-mass, wrath-math, and curve principles instead.
